issues.description: Behavioural change in _set_base_image silently overrides KFP's default image fallback
issues.detail: Previously, when pod introspection failed (NotInClusterError or ApiException), self.base_image was deliberately set to '' so that downstream code could fall through to KFP's own default. The diff now unconditionally writes DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE='python:3.12'. The precondition for that branch is 'we could not determine the running pod's image'; the postcondition has now silently changed from 'defer to KFP default' to 'pin to python:3.12'. No author has stated this precondition, no invariant has been written for which base_image value flows where, and no test demonstrates that the two regimes are equivalent. This is UNREASONED and TESTED-NOT-PROVED.

issues.description: The constant 'python:3.12' is duplicated in at least three places, violating single-source-of-truth
issues.detail: DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE is declared in backend/kale/pipeline.py, re-declared as a TypeScript constant in labextension/src/widgets/cell-metadata/CellMetadataEditor.tsx, and hardcoded again as a fallback string literal in Commands.getDefaultBaseImage's catch arm and in the Jinja template's prior history. The author cannot state an invariant 'there is exactly one place that defines the default base image' because the diff falsifies that invariant on introduction. When the Python value is bumped to python:3.13 nothing forces the TS literals to follow; the system will silently diverge.

issues.description: createBaseImageText conflates four distinct sources of truth into one opaque coalesce
issues.detail: The expression baseImage || pipelineBaseImage || defaultBaseImage || DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE has no stated invariant about which sources may legitimately be empty strings versus undefined, and the '(default)' label is computed solely from !baseImage so it is mislabelled whenever pipelineBaseImage is set (it will read 'Base Image: <pipeline image> (default)' even though the user explicitly chose a pipeline-level image). The precondition for the (default) annotation is never stated. This is a SMUGGLED-GOTO of state through a chain of fallbacks.

issues.description: getDefaultBaseImage swallows all exceptions and hides the failure mode behind a hardcoded literal
issues.detail: DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE. The try/catch returns 'python:3.12' for any error, conflating 'RPC unreachable', 'kernel busy', and 'server returned the wrong type' into a single silent success. A reader cannot derive the postcondition of getDefaultBaseImage from its source; they must inspect the network. State the precondition (kernel ready, RPC registered), state the postcondition (returns the server-defined default or raises), and either propagate the failure or render a visibly degraded state.

issues.description: An entire Input control was replaced by a modal Dialog with no stated justification
issues.detail: The previous UI exposed the base image as a one-shot Input element of width 25%. The new UI requires a click to open a Dialog, then a click to dismiss. No precondition, postcondition, or user-task argument has been stated for why an additional level of indirection is now correct. The 'Reset to Default' button writes the empty string, which then makes createBaseImageText display whichever upstream fallback wins; the user has no way to predict from the dialog which value will be shown. UNREASONED at the UX layer.

issues.description: Button style width:'5%' inside a flex/inline container is meaningless and likely wrong
issues.detail: A button labelled 'IMAGE' is given style={{ width: '5%' }} inside a div with marginRight 4px. The author cannot have reasoned about this number; 5% of what container, and why would a text-bearing button be one twentieth of any sensible width? This is the kind of magic number that survives only because it was never questioned.

issues.description: Local 'from kale.pipeline import DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE' inside get_default_base_image is gratuitous
issues.detail: The function performs a function-scope import of a module-level constant from a module that the surrounding rpc package already depends upon transitively. The justification (avoiding circular imports?) is unstated. If the precondition is 'we must defer this import to avoid a cycle', then the cycle should be named in a comment; otherwise the import belongs at module scope where every other reader can see what this file depends upon.

issues.description: No test demonstrates that the rendered DSL still compiles when default_base_image is supplied via the template context
issues.detail: The Jinja template was changed from a hardcoded 'python:3.12' literal to a template variable default_base_image. The author claims this is equivalent. Equivalence is not asserted by a test that renders the template under both the new compiler path and any legacy callers, and verifies the produced code is identical for steps without an explicit base image. Tested-not-proved at best; not even tested at worst.

review.summary: The change introduces a default base image constant and threads it from Python through an RPC into a redesigned React dialog. The headline defect is on the Python side: _set_base_image used to assign '' to fall through to KFP's own default and now silently pins python:3.12, a change of postcondition with no stated reasoning and no test. The single-source-of-truth invariant the author appears to want (one definition of the default) is violated on arrival by at least three duplicated literals across Python and TypeScript. The frontend rewrites a working Input into a modal Dialog without stating why indirection improves the user's task, and conflates four fallback sources into one coalesce whose '(default)' label is provably wrong when pipelineBaseImage is set. Verdict: REFUSED until the precondition/postcondition for _set_base_image, the single-source-of-truth for the default, and the precondition for the (default) annotation are stated and tested.
